submission.justification: Module-D2 gives the most light per unit coverage (38 PE/MeV at 20%). However, 30% of D2 modules failed after 20 thermal cycles because the bonding in the thin light guide cracks. That breaks the hard limit of 5% or fewer failures, and modules cannot be replaced, so D2 is ruled out. D1 (2% failed) and D3 (0.5% failed) both pass. D1 collects more light than D3 (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage). Light collection rises with coverage, so I chose the maximum allowed coverage of 30%. Feedthroughs for 30% are confirmed in the 2026-01-20 meeting notes. Using the 2025 scaling (coverage^0.8), D1 at 30% should give about 27*(30/20)^0.8 ≈ 37 PE/MeV. This is an extrapolation from the 2025 summary, not a new simulation run, because no simulation tool was available. D3 has a larger safety margin on failures, but D1 also meets the hard requirement and gives about 50% more light.

requirements.evidence: D1 is the highest-light design that meets the failure limit. Estimated ~37 PE/MeV at 30% coverage, extrapolated from the 2025 simulation (27 PE/MeV at 20%, scaling as coverage^0.8). Not confirmed by a new simulation.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: Thermal-cycling query and tests document: D1 had 2% failures in a 40-module batch. D2 (30%) fails this requirement; D3 (0.5%) passes.
30% chosen, the upper limit. The 2026-01-20 meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs for up to 30%.
